questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer:
I did have the privilege of experiencing the high-level research and academic excellence at Humboldt University in the field of medicinal chemistry. The university's state-of-the-art laboratories, advanced research facilities, and cutting-edge equipment created an ideal environment for groundbreaking discoveries and innovative advancements. During my time at Humboldt, I actively engaged in high-level research projects under the guidance of leading scientists in the field, which significantly enhanced my understanding and practical skills in medicinal chemistry.

One of the remarkable aspects of studying medicinal chemistry at Humboldt University was the emphasis on interdisciplinary collaborations. I had the opportunity to collaborate with experts from various fields such as pharmacology, biology, biochemistry, and drug discovery. This interdisciplinary approach provided me with a comprehensive understanding of the intricate relationship between chemical compounds and their therapeutic applications. Working alongside professionals from different scientific disciplines not only expanded my knowledge base but also enabled me to forge valuable connections and engage in cutting-edge research at the forefront of multiple fields.

Humboldt University's commitment to international collaborations and global perspective was truly inspiring. The university actively encouraged global exchanges, joint research projects, and collaborative initiatives with renowned institutions worldwide. I had the privilege of working with esteemed scientists from different countries, which broadened my horizons and exposed me to diverse perspectives and approaches. These international collaborations not only enriched my research experience but also nurtured my cultural understanding and equipped me to address complex challenges on an international scale as a globally-minded medicinal chemist.

The exceptional faculty at Humboldt University played a pivotal role in my academic and professional development. Working alongside distinguished scientists, renowned researchers, and accomplished professionals was a transformative experience. Their expertise, guidance, and support not only fostered my academic and research skills but also provided invaluable insights into the latest advancements and emerging trends in medicinal chemistry. The mentorship I received from these esteemed experts significantly shaped my educational experience and set me on a path towards success in the field.

The high ranking of Humboldt University in the global academic landscape further enhanced my educational journey. A degree from Humboldt carries significant prestige and recognition, which opened doors to a multitude of exciting career opportunities. The university's strong reputation attracted attention from renowned research organizations, pharmaceutical companies, and academic institutions worldwide. This exposure provided me with a competitive advantage in the job market, increasing my prospects for employment in prestigious positions within academia, industry, and research.

In conclusion, my experience at Humboldt University in the field of medicinal chemistry was truly transformative. The high-level research opportunities, interdisciplinary collaborations, international perspective, exceptional faculty, and the university's esteemed reputation have prepared me for a successful career in the field. I am immensely grateful for the invaluable knowledge, skills, and connections I gained during my time at Humboldt, which will undoubtedly shape my future endeavors as a medicinal chemist.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It was lot of pushing through the student coordination. No help at all. There were official description how to register but it was too complicated for foreign student to do. I had to pay tuition fee, involving money for "school groups" that are totally not implied for  me as Erasmus trainee student.
